title: Review of Liabilities and Penalties under Workplace Safety and Health Act
what_it_is: Review of Liabilities and Penalties under Workplace Safety and Health Act

sections.label: WSH Act reviews and programmes
sections.summary: The WSH Act, amended in 2008 and 2011, is under a third review, with MOM inspections, WSH Council education, safety training and company programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower
sentences.text: Since its enactment in 2006, it was amended in 2008 and 2011.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower
sentences.text: We have started a third review since earlier this year and aim to complete it before the end of the year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower
sentences.text: On enforcement, MOM conducts more than 16,000 inspections per year, as mentioned earlier just now.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower
sentences.text: On awareness, the Workplace Safety and Health Council, where SNEF and NTUC are represented, has conducted education programmes reaching out to 500,000 workers a year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower
sentences.text: On training, more than 150,000 workers undergo safety training every year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower
sentences.text: The Workplace Safety and Health Council is also partnering SkillsFuture Singapore to enhance the	Workplace Safety and Health (WSH) training curriculum of workers, supervisors and managers over the next two years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower
sentences.text: As of 2016, over 27,000 companies have benefited from these programmes.

sections.label: Proposed changes in current review
sections.summary: The proposed changes in the current review aim to strengthen industry ownership and enhance deterrence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: With regard to the second supplementary question by the Member on what the proposed changes in the current review are, the proposed changes aim to strengthen industry ownership and also to enhance deterrence.

sections.label: Maximum penalty under subsidiary legislation
sections.summary: The last area of review is to increase the maximum penalty under the WSH Act's subsidiary legislation for offences causing serious injuries or death.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: The last area of review is to increase the maximum penalty under the WSH Act's subsidiary legislation for offences that could result in serious injuries or even death.
